speakers: Mike Pile (deputy head of BlackRock portfolio management group, ex-global CIO strategist, ex-US deputy national security adviser for international economics)
summary:
Interview with BlackRock's Mike Pile on the shift from the demand-driven 2010s to a supply-driven, scarcity regime (AI buildout, energy shocks, active fiscal).
He argues bonds now serve as income not duration diversification, so 60/40 should become growth core + income + market-neutral diversifiers, with systematic multistrategy at the core of hedge fund allocation.
AI-supply-chain earnings are bottleneck-driven but valuations are modest; AI is also raising breadth in research.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: a world shaped by supply
claims.claim: Today's macro regime is driven by supply-side shocks (war, energy, AI capex) rather than the lack of aggregate demand that characterised the 2010s, which changes policy, volatility regime and portfolio construction.
claims.testable: partly: regime classification is judgmental but can be proxied by inflation vs growth shocks

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: that's a world where stocks and bonds are going to are going to co-move uh differently than in a world where inflation is a bigger risk
claims.claim: When growth is the dominant worry stocks and bonds co-move differently (negative correlation) than when inflation is the bigger risk, so the stock-bond correlation depends on the growth-vs-inflation regime.
claims.direction: bonds hedge stocks when growth risk dominates
claims.testable: yes: rolling stock-bond correlation vs inflation regime

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: really dramatically suppressing or lowering economic volatility as well as market volatility
claims.claim: Pinning rates at the floor and QE in the 2010s suppressed both economic and market volatility.
claims.testable: partly: vol suppression measurable, attribution to policy is not

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: we saw really nice diversification properties uh in the 2010s where bonds were a really great hedge to stocks uh because of that negative stock bond correlation driven fundamentally by growth risks being predominant
claims.claim: In the 2010s bonds were a strong hedge for stocks because the stock-bond correlation was negative, driven by dominant growth risks.
claims.testable: yes: correlation and hedge performance history

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: market dispersion uh was was really compressed
claims.claim: Policy-suppressed volatility compressed cross-sectional market dispersion, shrinking the alpha opportunity set for active and hedge fund managers.
claims.testable: yes: dispersion vs active/hedge fund returns

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: what was rewarded frankly both on the on the uh fixed income side as well as the equity side were sort of quote unquote kind of long duration trades
claims.claim: In the zero-rate 2010s long-duration assets (long bonds, risk parity, long-dated-cash-flow tech growth equities) were rewarded on both bond and equity sides.
claims.testable: yes: duration factor returns by rate regime

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: policy makers similarly run the risk of always you know fighting the last crisis
claims.claim: Policymakers react to the previous crisis: after the GFC fiscal response was seen as too small, so the 2020s response was large fiscal activism.
claims.testable: no: narrative about policy reaction function

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: fiscal policy, you know, can move the lever and and and and accelerate uh economies back towards
claims.claim: The 2016-2020 recovery, helped by the early-Trump fiscal expansion, showed that fiscal policy can pull economies back to potential, reinforcing fiscal activism.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: the risk is doing too little rather than doing too much
claims.claim: Biden-era policymakers saw the risk as doing too little (scarring) rather than too much, but then found there are risks on the other side (inflation).

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: we're living in a world of of of of scarcity
claims.claim: A supply-driven world is a world of scarcity (supply chains, energy, inputs), in contrast to the abundance of capital and demand-weakness of the 2010s.
claims.testable: partly: scarcity proxies (supply chain pressure indices, commodity prices)

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: seeing a a number of bottlenecks emerge just in terms of real resources
claims.claim: The AI buildout is creating real-resource bottlenecks (leading-edge chips, energy and other inputs) that add to scarcity.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: That's a lot of demands uh that we're placing on capital markets today and I think that that's leading to um you know the the types of interest rate dynamics
claims.claim: Heavy demands on capital markets (AI buildout, government deficits, IG corporates, housing, consumer finance) push up interest rates.
claims.conditions: when capital demand exceeds saving supply

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: when does some of this AI buildout uh flip us from more of a scarcity paradigm into one of abundance
claims.claim: The key macro question is when AI investment shifts the regime from scarcity to abundance via productivity gains.
claims.conditions: if AI productivity outweighs resource demands

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: we have we have extraordinary real-time capabilities to uh gather data
claims.claim: Because AI forecasts are highly uncertain, policymakers and investors should watch real-time data to see whether the productivity handoff is happening rather than rely on forecasts.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: the evidence thus far is fragmentaryary
claims.claim: Evidence of AI productivity gains is so far fragmentary: incremental investment is producing incremental corporate earnings, but not yet enough to outweigh resource demands of the buildout.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: the pressure is upward on inflation uh and rates
claims.claim: Near term, real-resource and capital-market needs of the AI, resilience and fiscal buildouts put upward pressure on inflation and rates.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: estimating the the real equilibrium rates a pretty hard business and even which direction it's moving I think is a pretty hard business
claims.claim: Technology-driven productivity is disinflationary (1990s analogy) but could raise or lower the real neutral rate; neither level nor direction of r-star is reliably estimable.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: I do think that we can have you know some confidence that there's there's a disinflationary trend uh ahead
claims.claim: The speaker has some confidence in a medium-term disinflationary trend from productivity-enhancing technology.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: they're trading under you know 10 times uh forward earnings
claims.claim: Forward valuations of AI-theme companies are not stretched (memory firms under 10x forward earnings), unlike the late-1990s bubble.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: it's been the companies to whom the hyperscalers have been writing checks
claims.claim: In 2026 hyperscaler stocks lagged while the suppliers receiving their capex (chokepoint companies) led equity returns.
claims.indicator: AI capex supplier stocks vs hyperscalers

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: in the short run, factors of production are fixed. In the long run, factors of production, uh, you know, are flexible and move to where opportunity are
claims.claim: Bottleneck-driven extraordinary profits dissipate over quarters to years as supply expands and new entrants arrive, because factors of production are fixed only in the short run.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: I would expect that those multiples retrade higher
claims.claim: Low multiples on peak earnings reflect market scepticism over durability; once sustainable earnings become visible, multiples should re-rate higher.
claims.direction: multiples rise as earnings visibility improves

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: the demand for AI capabilities is outstripping supply however much we're building out
claims.claim: Demand for AI capability still exceeds supply, implying continued buildout and a healthy, though lower than peak, earnings trajectory.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: we continue to be really across the platform uh on balance uh overweight uh US equities
claims.claim: BlackRock keeps growth equity exposure (US equities, technology/AI) as portfolio core, overweight US equities, sized appropriately.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: bonds can be a really significant source of income uh in a portfolio
claims.claim: Bonds' role has shifted from duration diversifier to income source, so portfolios should favour income over duration.
claims.direction: hold bonds for income not hedging
claims.conditions: when stock-bond correlation is not reliably negative
claims.testable: partly: backtest income vs duration roles

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: we've shifted from a world of of you know more durationoriented fixed income portfolios to more income uh portfolios
claims.claim: Move from duration-oriented fixed income to income portfolios in corporate credit, EM credit and private markets.
claims.direction: long corporate and EM credit, private credit

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: diversification is in relatively short supply in terms of today's market landscape
claims.claim: Diversification is scarce now, so market-neutral low-net alpha strategies have a bigger role.
claims.direction: add market-neutral hedge funds / liquid alts
claims.conditions: when bonds no longer hedge equities
claims.testable: partly: correlation to equity and bond

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: bringing public and private exposures together
claims.claim: A sound diversified income portfolio needs public and private credit, infrastructure and securitized/EM exposures together, because public markets alone miss attractive income assets.
claims.direction: private credit and infrastructure for income

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: running at kind of low or zero beta is, you know, a really important thing to add to the mix of a total portfolio
claims.claim: Market-neutral low-net hedge fund strategies should be treated as diversifiers because their zero-beta return stream is less sensitive to growth swings than equity and income exposures.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: it's really a lot of those more market neutral type exposures that can provide the best diversification potential
claims.claim: Market-neutral strategies are not as straightforward a diversifier as the 10-year Treasury was a decade ago, but are the best remaining diversification source.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: as we know from the fundamental law of active management uh higher breath is uh is a is an important ingredient in building a high stable information ratio
claims.claim: Multi-strategy pooling of many alpha streams raises breadth and so, by the fundamental law of active management, information ratio.
claims.testable: yes: IR scales with breadth when alphas independent

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: reallocate across those strategies dynamically, you know, in the face of changing market conditions not really available
claims.claim: A multi-strategy manager can reallocate dynamically across alpha streams, which an end investor combining separate funds cannot replicate; systematic managers have an edge here.
claims.direction: use a multistrategy manager as core

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: complementing that with you know additional strategies can can also make sense you know more um directional uh macro or long short uh equity strategies
claims.claim: Directional macro and long-short equity satellites around a systematic multistrategy core change the risk/return and correlation shape, e.g. for stress environments.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: those factor exposures are actually subject to really unattractive draw down uh features in stressed markets
claims.claim: Pre-2007 quant strategies harvested factor exposures, which suffered large drawdowns in stress (quant crisis).

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: dial some of those well-known uh factor exposures like momentum, like others as close to zero as possible
claims.claim: Post-quant-crisis, BlackRock systematic neutralises beta and well-known factor exposures (e.g. momentum) to isolate pure alpha, which makes portfolios more resilient.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: the momentum trade in in AI there was a big reversal and then obviously we saw in one case hedge fund hitting margin calls
claims.claim: A recent AI momentum reversal caused a hedge fund to hit margin calls, echoing leverage stress of the 2007 quant crisis.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: that type of approach uh makes these portfolios much more resilient uh across time than you know what we saw prior uh to the GFC
claims.claim: Beta- and factor-neutralised portfolio construction has been more resilient in moderate stress episodes since the GFC.
claims.testable: partly: evidence from modest stress episodes only

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: that combination of um the widespread availability of diversification and the compressed opportunity set at a macro level kind of really explains why uh that was such a challenged uh period of time for the hedge fund landscape
claims.claim: The 2010s were poor for hedge funds because cheap diversification (long bonds) was abundant while dispersion and the alpha opportunity set were compressed.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: markets are offering greater dispersion as a result greater opportunity to generate alpha particularly in long short strategies
claims.claim: Today diversification is scarce and dispersion is larger, which supports hedge fund performance, especially long-short, and allocators returning to them.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: allocators didn't want to give up their equity beta
claims.claim: Allocators hesitated to buy hedge funds that lagged equities and hedge fund track records look better when combined with equity beta, driving interest in extension and portable alpha.
claims.direction: portable alpha: beta plus market-neutral alpha

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: long only strategies um you know face a range of challenges um you know delivering alpha as a general matter not in all cases uh because of how concentrated um equity markets uh have become
claims.claim: Concentrated equity markets make it hard for long-only active managers to deliver alpha; adding shorts lets managers exploit dispersion.
claims.testable: yes: long-only active alpha vs concentration

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: you're getting your beta exposure and then you're porting on top of that a long short um you know market neutral strategy
claims.claim: Portable alpha separates beta (index vehicle) from alpha (market-neutral long-short overlay) rather than embedding both in a long-only mandate.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: moving away from a traditional 60/40
claims.claim: Replace 60/40 with growth equity core, income-focused diversified fixed income across public and private markets, and diversifiers such as market-neutral hedge funds and liquid alts.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: it's important to um move beyond uh asset classes and to think very distinctly across asset classes about what the distinct drivers of risk and return are
claims.claim: Total portfolio approach builds portfolios around underlying risk drivers or themes (growth/AI, duration, income) rather than asset-class buckets.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: they were doing natural language processing more than a decade ago
claims.claim: Systematic teams have used NLP and machine learning for alpha signals and portfolio construction for over a decade.

claims.speaker: Mike Pile
claims.quote: it's going to be about building more breadth into fundamental portfolios
claims.claim: AI tools should increase analyst coverage and idea velocity on the fundamental side, raising breadth, which with forecast quality drives active results.
